note: Attacker-controlled JSON input (top-level object {"Type":22,"Body":{...}}) is dispatched to Variant_decodeJson; the parsed token stream enters the vulnerable flow here.
The "Type":22 field resolves via UA_findDataType to UA_TYPES_EXTENSIONOBJECT, selecting the ExtensionObject unwrap decode path for the Variant body.
The ExtensionObject body object is delegated to Variant_decodeJsonUnwrapExtensionObject, which allocates storage for the inner value.
TypeId "Id":6 resolves to UA_TYPES_INT32; UA_new allocates the body object and stores it in dst->data with dst->type set.

The inner body decode fails ("Body":"abc" is not a valid Int32 JSON primitive), so the error branch frees dst->data but does not reset it to NULL, leaving a dangling pointer recorded in the Variant (missing ownership/lifetime enforcement).
The decode error propagates to UA_decodeJson, whose cleanup calls UA_deleteMembers on the partially decoded Variant that still references the already-freed dst->data pointer.
Cleanup reaches Variant_clear: since p->type is set and the dangling p->data is above UA_EMPTY_ARRAY_SENTINEL, UA_Array_delete frees the same allocation a second time, causing the double-free.
